signature: SUBROUTINE ZHGEQZ( JOB, COMPQ, COMPZ, N, ILO, IHI, H, LDH, T, LDT,

params.name: job
params.reference:
-   `= 'E'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
-   `= 'S'`: Computer eigenvalues and the Schur form.

params.name: compq
compz
N
params.reference: The order of the matrices H, T, Q, and Z. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: ihi
params.reference: `ILO` and `IHI` mark the rows and columns of H which are in Hessenberg form. It is assumed that A is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N. If $N > 0$, $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$; if $N = 0$, `ILO=1` and `IHI=0`.

params.name: H
params.reference: On entry, the N-by-N upper Hessenberg matrix H. On exit, if `JOB = 'S'`, H contains the upper triangular matrix S from the generalized Schur factorization. If `JOB = 'E'`, the diagonal of H matches that of S, but the rest of H is unspecified.

params.name: ldh
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array H. $\mathrm{LDH} \ge \max ( 1, N )$.

params.name: T
params.reference: On entry, the N-by-N upper triangular matrix T. On exit, if `JOB = 'S'`, T contains the upper triangular matrix P from the generalized Schur factorization. If `JOB = 'E'`, the diagonal of T matches that of P, but the rest of T is unspecified.

params.name: ldt
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array T. $\mathrm{LDT} \ge \max ( 1, N )$.

params.name: ALPHA
params.reference: The complex scalars $\alpha$ that define the eigenvalues of GNEP. `ALPHA(i) = S(i,i)` in the generalized Schur factorization.

params.name: BETA
params.reference:
The real non-negative scalars $\beta$ that define the eigenvalues of GNEP. `BETA(i) = P(i,i)` in the generalized Schur factorization.

Together, the quantities $\alpha = \mathrm{ALPHA}(j)$ and $\beta = \mathrm{BETA}(j)$ represent the j-th eigenvalue of the matrix pair (A,B), in one of the forms $\lambda = \alpha /\beta$ or $\mu = \beta /\alpha$. Since either $\lambda$ or $\mu$ may overflow, they should not, in general, be computed.

params.name: Q
params.reference: On entry, if `COMPQ = 'V'`, the unitary matrix Q1 used in the reduction of (A,B) to generalized Hessenberg form. On exit, if `COMPQ = 'I'`, the unitary matrix of left Schur vectors of (H,T), and if `COMPQ = 'V'`, the unitary matrix of left Schur vectors of (A,B). Not referenced if `COMPQ = 'N'`.

params.name: ldq
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array Q. $\mathrm{LDQ} \ge 1$. If `COMPQ='V'` or 'I', then $\mathrm{LDQ} \ge N$.

params.name: Z
params.reference: On entry, if `COMPZ = 'V'`, the unitary matrix Z1 used in the reduction of (A,B) to generalized Hessenberg form. On exit, if `COMPZ = 'I'`, the unitary matrix of right Schur vectors of (H,T), and if `COMPZ = 'V'`, the unitary matrix of right Schur vectors of (A,B). Not referenced if `COMPZ = 'N'`.

params.name: ldz
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array Z. $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge 1$. If `COMPZ='V'` or 'I', then $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge N$.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if $\mathrm{INFO} \ge 0$, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,N)$.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `= 1,...,N`: the QZ iteration did not converge.  (H,T) is not in Schur form, but `ALPHA(i)` and `BETA(i)`, $i=\mathrm{INFO}+1$,...,N should be correct. = N+1,...,$2 \, N$: the shift calculation failed.  (H,T) is not in Schur form, but `ALPHA(i)` and `BETA(i)`, $i=\mathrm{INFO}-N+1$,...,N should be correct.
